data.content_ref: inline:The proposed relation is 'integrates with ... by removing the authoring trace but failing to remove the shared priors.' But what is REFUTED IF — 'a complete context wipe allows a single engine to identify a systemic hallucination that it previously authored' — targets a capability that would be present even with no integration at all: an engine catching its own hallucination after a context wipe doesn't falsify an integration claim between statelessness and cognitive covariance theory, it merely describes a positive detection outcome. The refutation condition is disconnected from the asserted relation: it tests whether self-correction succeeds, not whether the integration-via-shared-priors claim fails. A genuine refutation would need to show shared priors were absent or irrelevant, not that a hallucination was detected.
